s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure
salient_findings: Erythema and helical thickening with numerous small blisters on ears
Vesicles at the upper and lower vermillion border
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient reported malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Laboratory tests showed detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
Erythematous papules and crusts located on cheeks, neck, and lower arms

shortlist.label: Parvovirus B19-associated erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erythematous papules, crusts, and vesicles on sun-exposed areas

shortlist.label: Phototoxic reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure

shortlist.label: Solar urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic skin eruption with erythema and vesicles after sun exposure

shortlist.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of vesicles and erythema on sun-exposed areas

shortlist.label: Actinic prurigo
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic skin eruption with erythema and papules on sun-exposed areas

shortlist.label: Phytophotodermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with erythema and vesicles after sun exposure, possibly due to plant contact

raw.rationale: The presence of detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in the lesional skin biopsy specimen, along with the patient's symptoms of malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation, support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the patient had a skin eruption after sun exposure, the presence of PVB19 DNA and antibodies points more specifically to a viral etiology

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: This condition is often associated with herpes simplex virus or other infections, but the virologic analyses were negative for these

rejected.label: Phototoxic reaction
rejected.why: The patient had no history of photosensitivity and denied the use of any topical or systemic photosensitizers

rejected.label: Solar urticaria
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic wheals of solar urticaria

rejected.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more severe blistering and scarring, which is not described in the patient's case

rejected.label: Actinic prurigo
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic intense pruritus and the distribution of lesions is not typical for actinic prurigo

rejected.label: Phytophotodermatitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of plant exposure, which is a necessary component of this diagnosis
